fatal_errors: The hypothesis does not identify the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA, its L12/B2 lamellar microstructure, or the DS2205 comparator.
It replaces the matched thermal-shock and temperature-dependent comparison with an unspecified untreated-HEA baseline.
The proposed 3.5% NaCl, 10 N, and 0.1 m/s conditions do not reconstruct the deionized-water reciprocating tests or the critical 25–100 °C temperature comparison.

Grain refinement is asserted as the governing mediator even though the target mechanism depends on retained phase structure, passive-film repair, tribo-layer stability, and temperature-dependent changes in wear mode.
The claimed 20%, 15%, and 30% reductions are unsupported by the cited evidence and inconsistent with the observed approximately order-of-magnitude wear-rate advantage over DS2205.
The hypothesis misses the non-monotonic temperature response, with minimum degradation near 50 °C and greater degradation at both 25 and 100 °C.
The proposed experiment does not directly manipulate or measure passive-film repair, grain refinement, or tribo-layer stability, so it cannot isolate the alleged governing cause.
The cited studies largely concern tensile properties, irradiation, heat treatment, or separate wear and corrosion behavior rather than coupled tribo-corrosion under the proposed conditions.
explanation: The response recognizes that passive-film behavior can couple wear and corrosion, but otherwise provides a generic and largely unsubstantiated hypothesis. It fails to reconstruct the alloy, DS2205 baseline, rapid heating/quenching treatment, immersed reciprocating configuration, deionized-water conditions, or temperature-governed transition among abrasion, polishing, and oxide/third-body wear. Its quantitative predictions and grain-size/passive-layer boundaries are invented rather than derived from the evidence. Although it gives a nominal falsification threshold, varying load and speed would test performance trends rather than discriminate the proposed passive-layer/grain-refinement mechanism.
